headline: Awami League’s violence and sabotage: Administration must establish control

members.title: Gopalganj university remains open, but all classes and exams suspended
members.lead: The administration of Gopalganj Science and Technology University has suspended all classes and examinations over security concerns. The decision was announced in a notice issued on Thursday in view of the overall situation in Gopalganj. The notice, signed by acting registrar and Regent Board (the university’s highest policymaking and governing body) secretary Morad Hossain, said the decision would take effect from 22 November. The notice stated that all academic activities at the university would remain suspended until further notice. However, vice-chancellor of the university Sohel Hasan said the university would remain open. The notice said that, following a decision taken at the Regent Board’s sixth emergency meeting on 17 November, all classes and examinations at the university had been suspended on 18 and 19 November. .Gopalganj: Traffic resumes on highway after 36 hours. In continuation of that decision, classes and examinations had now been suspended again, taking into account the overall situation in the district and at the university as well as students’ safety, added the notice. The university administration’s decision has renewed concerns about security on the campus. Political tensions, protests and various violent incidents in Gopalganj over the past few days have disrupted normalcy. . Since Thursday morning, several processions carrying locally made weapons had taken place in front of the university’s main gate over the activities-banned Awami League’s call for a lockdown programme. . Amid this situation, leaders and activists of the banned Chhatra League entered the campus through the main gate at noon on Thursday and staged a procession, chanting slogans. Earlier, Chhatra League leaders and activists had put up a signboard at the university’s main gate bearing the name ‘Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Science and Technology University’. . members.title: Awami League’s violence and sabotage: Administration must establish control
members.lead: The violence and chaos sparked by the recent programmes called by Awami League (activities banned in the country) have left people feeling anxious and worried. While their disruptive acts have spread to several districts, the situation in Gopalganj has gone out of hand. So far, the government has chosen to show restraint in handling the unrest. We certainly welcome this stance. But saboteurs might exploit the situation if law enforcement agencies sit back for too long. The government needs to realise that this kind of situation cannot just linger on indefinitely. They must come up with effective strategies to restore peace and make sure citizens' lives and properties are safe. According to Prothom Alo's reports, acts of sabotage hit 17 districts starting Tuesday night all the way through Wednesday midnight, and the chaos rolled right into Thursday. In different areas, Awami League activists torched buses, railway lines, BNP offices and even lawmakers' homes. Grameen Bank offices were set on fire in various parts of the country. Dhaka saw a few crude bomb explosions too. . These last few days of violence and attacks have already claimed four lives. In Pirojpur, a bus driver’s assistant was burned to death while sleeping inside his vehicle when it was torched. In Narail's Kalia, two people were killed when Awami League men attacked a BNP procession. A Krishak Dal member lost his life in Faridpur. The most worrying situation is unfolding in Gopalganj. Awami League leaders and activists kept up non-stop violence across the entire district, including Tungipara and Gopalganj Sadar from Tuesday evening until Thursday evening, when this piece was being written. Tungipara Police Station had to shut down operations after being torched. Muksudpur Police Station was attacked and burned as well. The houses of BNP MPs Selimuzzaman Molla, KM Babar and SM Jilani were targeted, vandalised and set ablaze, alongside a hospital owned by an MP. Even police and BGB vehicles were targeted…

members.title: If you burn down police stations, how will police work: IGP in Gopalganj
members.lead: Seeking locals' cooperation in maintaining law and order in Gopalganj, Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir said, “If you burn down your police stations, how will the police work to maintain law and order?” He said, “If you think the police are not needed, then you will have to ensure your own security.” The IGP made the remarks while answering questions from journalists after attending a meeting on the law and order situation in the district at the Circuit House in Gopalganj town on Friday. .Gopalganj university remains open, but all classes and exams suspended.Activities-banned Awami League holds protest march in Gopalganj with machetes, hockey sticks. IGP Ali Hossain said, “I believe you (the people of Gopalganj) will cooperate with the police force and other law enforcement agencies in maintaining peace and order in the area.” Speaking about the law and order situation in Gopalganj, the IGP said, “I find the overall situation quite good as of today. It will remain good in the coming days as well.” Addressing local residents, he said, “All of you should unite and stand against those who create unrest among peace-loving people. The number of such people is not very large.” Replying to a query about resuming operations at the two police stations that were set on fire, the police chief said, “Who are these police stations for? They are for you, for the people. If you burn down your police stations, how will they (the police) work? If you do not cooperate with the police, they will not be able to work. And if you want no police, you will have to maintain law and order yourselves.” . Asked whether any operation would be conducted to arrest those involved in the recent violence, the IGP said, “The main thing is that the government will decide what the people want.” Asked about the announcement of programmes by the activities-banned Awami League, the police chief said, “You have seen before that there have been many consecutive programmes.
